Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it was helpful to see the streaming and prefix cache behavior in action. A few follow-ups from the product and security teams here at OliveHealth as we scope a two-week hosted pilot: 

- Traffic profile: ~200 QPS peak for a 2-hour morning window, baseline ~12 QPS otherwise.
- Data classification: the payloads will include semi-structured patient summaries (no raw PHI uploads; some de-identified identifiers). We need clarity on logs/audit retention and whether logs can be disabled on hosted for the pilot.
- Rate caps & endpoints: we want a staging URL and a canary path (10% traffic) that points at the new model. Can you confirm how rate limits apply per-token vs per-request and how burst behavior is handled?
- Rollout behavior: on Canary failover we need an automatic fallback to a smaller LLM variant (faster but lower quality).

Attached: demo-recording-20280324.mp4 (recording + timestamp notes).

Proposed timeline: staging token and a configuration doc by EOD Friday would let our engineers start smoke tests next week. Also looping procurement on this thread — they may need a short MSA for the pilot.

Can you confirm next steps and any known blockers for hosted as the first-path deployment?

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Product — OliveHealth

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Hi Samir — great to chat. Quick answers and clear next steps below.

1) Staging & tokens
- We'll provision a staging API key scoped to your account and three sandbox endpoints: /v1/stream, /v1/batch, /v1/embeddings. Expected ETA: staging token by 2028-03-26 11:00 PT.

2) Rate limits & bursts
- Default pilot plan: soft cap at 300 requests/minute per endpoint, with token-based throttling for sustained usage. Short bursts (up to 2x) allowed for up to 30s; sustained bursts will be throttled. We'll provide a ratecap header so your client can adapt.

3) Canary and automatic fallback
- We can configure a 10% canary route. On error rate > 5% or latency > 2s for 3 consecutive checks, Canary will automatically roll back traffic to the designated fallback model (we recommend a quantized gpt-small variant).

4) Logs & audit retention
- Hosted keeps request/response metadata for 30 days by default. For the pilot we can disable response payload retention and only keep request headers and aggregated metrics. This is sufficient for smoke testing but not for full SOC-level evidence — security will flag that for longer-term.

Next steps (what I'll deliver):
- staging token + sandbox endpoints (attachment: hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf)
- a short runbook for canary config and rollback thresholds
- HubSpot note with the pilot config (I'll include the URL below)

Can you confirm the traffic windows and whether your engineers can accept the soft caps above for initial tests? If procurement needs an MSA for pilot access we can provide a short-term addendum.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Strategic Solutions, Redwood Inference
